newsitem.title: ITALY: Sicilian mafia boss says he killed magistrate.
newsitem.headline: Sicilian mafia boss says he killed magistrate.

text.p: Mob boss Giovanni Brusca told a Sicilian court on Thursday that he detonated explosives which killed star anti-mafia magistrate Giovanni Falcone, his wife and three bodyguards in 1992.
"I am guilty. I pressed the remote control button," said Brusca, who has cooperated with authorities since his arrest last May, in the fortified prison courtroom.
Italian television news showed several prison guards surrounding the seated Brusca and shielding his face from view as he confirmed his role in the murder.

Brusca said the killing of Falcone, whose car was blown up on a motorway outside Palermo as it sped across a culvert packed with explosives, was carried out after previous Mafia attempts to assassinate the judge had failed.
He said the attack was also a message to former prime minister Giulio Andreotti from the Mafia. Brusca said they felt that the politician had betrayed them.
Andreotti, who was prime minister seven times, has been on trial in Palermo since late 1994 on charges that he was the Mafia's chief political protector for more than a decade.
The 78-year-old life senator denies allegations that he helped fix trials and obtain other favours for the Mafia in return for support in Sicily.
Brusca was testifying at a trial in central Sicily for those charged with Falcone's murder.
As he entered the courtroom, one of the accused, Leoluca Bagarella, commented "The pig has arrived".
Although Brusca has been cooperating with magistrates, investigators have doubts about his sincerity.
He has not been given access to Italy's witness protection scheme while anti-Mafia magistrates decide whether he is a "fake turncoat" who has been deliberately trying to mislead them.
Brusca admitted on Thursday that he had lied at the start of his collaboration "to save two people" and had considered misleading investigators.
But he said he now intended to "tell all the truth".
